correctness.rationale: Theorem 4.5 and Proposition 4.9 of arXiv:1708.02351 justify the weight-three reduced integral model. The basis count is C(8,k)2^k C(14-k,3-k), giving 364,1248,1344,448. A unit pivot clears its row by integral column additions, then its column by integral row additions; a zero residual gives saturated image, and the homology subgroup of the corresponding free cokernel is free. Connectedness can also be proved directly in the reduced model: degree-one relations exchange adjacent edge variables in degree-three multisets; the line graph is connected, so all degree-three monomials represent the same class in H0. Independently, using Prue–Scrimshaw's once-bisected cubical model, I enumerated (1140,3672,3840,1296) cells, checked both integral boundary squares, and removed all 1296 cubes by free face pairs. Contracting a spanning tree of 1139 edges gave 2533 one-cells and 2544 two-cells; 2527 exact unit pivots and zero residual yield H1=Z^6 and H2=Z^17, and the spine gives the higher vanishing. Replay: python3 /tmp/opencode/graph_triples_audit.py. Neither calculation relies on modular ranks for the absence of torsion.
